Meta.description: A personal game library, kept on a lit shelf you can walk along.

Foundations.title: Foundations
Foundations.lead: What Shelf is built from: light, color, type and motion, shown on blank cases.

hero.description: A backlit shelf of blank game cases, facing out
hero.hint: Point at a case, or touch one. The shelf's light takes its color.

light.title: Light
light.body: A theme is a lighting state, not an inversion. Lights on: daylight, and each shelf's LED bar is a thin line. Lights off: the LEDs carry the room.
light.sceneLabel: A shelf of blank game cases facing out, {time, select, day {with the room lights on} other {lit only by its LED bar}}
light.choose: It follows your device until you choose.

led.label: LED color
led.hint: On the real shelf, the light follows the game in focus.

color.title: Color
color.body: The games supply the color, so the room stays neutral: near-black or pale gray, one accent, and a light that changes.

type.title: Type
type.body: Two families. Archivo does titles and interface: a wide, heavy cut for titles, the regular one for everything else. Martian Mono does numbers and labels.
type.display: Archivo, wide and heavy, for titles
type.sansSample: Add games from IGDB, then find any of them with filters you can combine, save and share.
type.mono: Martian Mono, for numbers and labels

motion.title: Motion
motion.body: Quick and exact: things snap to attention and settle. Nothing bounces. Five lengths cover everything.
motion.calm: Your device asks for reduced motion, so these jump into place.

controls.title: Controls
controls.body: Built on Radix primitives and restyled. Focus is always an accent ring.

Landing.metaTitle: Shelf: every game you own, on one shelf
Landing.metaDescription: Put every game you own on one lit shelf, physical and digital, from every console. Find the next one to play with a line of text. Free.
Landing.shareAlt: “Every game you own, on one shelf.” beside three lit shelves of game boxes.

hero.eyebrow: For people with a lot of games
hero.title: Every game you own, on one shelf.
hero.lead: Physical and digital, every console and every generation, lit like the shelf you always wanted. Find the next one to play in a second.
hero.note: Free. Your shelf is ready in a minute.
hero.shelf: An example shelf of {count, number} games, facing out and lit from behind

ask.title: Ask it anything.
ask.body: One line finds any game: whether you started it, how long it takes, what it plays on. Save the line, and it becomes a shelf of its own.
ask.none: Nothing here matches. Try another line.

copies.title: One game. Every copy.
copies.body: On disc years ago, again in a sale, once more for the Switch? It stands on your shelf once, with every copy you own in the case it came in.
copies.together: One box, {count, plural, one {# copy} other {# copies}} in it

add.title: Add a game in seconds. Or a hundred.
add.body: Type a few letters and pick it by its cover. Or paste a whole list, a game on each line, and check the matches. Covers, years and lengths come with every game.

views.title: Shelf, wall or list.
views.body: Walk it as a shelf, scan it as a wall of covers, or sort it as a list of numbers. On a computer, the shelf can stand in 3D.
views.label: View

finished.title: See how far you got.
finished.body: Mark a game finished and it goes up on your trophy wall, under its own light, in the year you finished it. Above it: how many, how many hours, and what you made of them.
finished.wall: Games finished on the example shelf

privacy.title: Yours to show, or to keep.
privacy.body: You choose when you sign up, and can change it any time.

public.title: Public
public.body: Anyone can look, and search engines can list it. Nobody but you can change a thing.

private.title: Private
private.body: Only you can see it: not other people, not search engines.

privacy.notes: Notes you write about a game stay private, on a public shelf too, unless you mark them public.

assistant.title: Ask your assistant what to play.
assistant.body: Connect Claude, or another AI assistant that supports MCP, to your shelf. It reads your games and answers from them, and adds the ones you tell it about.
assistant.question: Something short I haven't started, that I can play on the Switch?
assistant.answer: {count, plural, one {One game on your shelf fits:} other {# games on your shelf fit:}}
assistant.pick: {platform} · about {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}

closing.label: Your shelf
closing.title: Your shelf is waiting.
closing.body: Free, and ready in a minute. Bring every game you own.

free.a: Yes. Making a shelf and keeping your games on it costs nothing.

data.q: Where does the information about games come from?
data.a: From IGDB.com: titles, covers, release dates, and how long games take to finish. What is yours you add: where you own a game, how far you got, what you thought of it.

who.a: You choose when you sign up, and can change it any time on your account page. A public shelf is for anyone, and search engines can list it; a private one is for you alone. Notes stay private unless you mark them public, game by game.

export.q: Can I take my games with me?
export.a: Your whole library can be read through Shelf's API while you are signed in. A one-click export is planned.
